sources: Wikipedia — It's Goin' Down (Yung Joc song): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_Goin%27_Down_(Yung_Joc_song)
notes: Snap with a keyboard hook instead of a chant hook, which the research states as the lane distinction and which shows up here as note density: `melody.densityPerBar` [4, 8] against the archetype's [2, 5], `emptyBarBias` 0.02, and an `arrangement` whose intro is the riff alone — "the riff never stops". The kit is the documented "clicking drumbeat": the snare is replaced by a thin clicky layer, so `percs.lanes` leads with `rim` at −5 dB beside the snap, `layerClapOffsetMs` collapses to [0, 2] so the two read as one click, and `velocityTiers` sit a notch under the archetype's — the "popping sound in the place of the snare drum" is quiet, not loud. The kick is the lane's own figure, 1 and the "&" of 3, pinned at two hits with `offbeat8thShare` 0.34. ⚠ **`confidence` is medium because the research rates it high-medium**, and the parameter that is inferred is the tempo: the beat's described elements and the Nitti credit are sourced, the 70–80 half-time band is marked [LOW-CONF], so `session.bpm` 140–160 is the inference. ⛔ **This model and `nitti` describe the same record from two directions and are deliberately not the same file.** The artist entry is the catalog — 1–2 bar loops, a hook block, some variation at the phrase end; the producer entry is the workflow, where repetition-without-development is the authored parameter and `melody.endVariation` is false. If they ever converge, the artist is the one that should move. ⚠ `chords` is a single line implying `i` with a passing `VII`, which is exactly the two families here; the variety the chord part owes comes from `chordDurationBeats` [3, 12] and a 30-semitone voicing register, not from progressions the record does not play. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
